data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Kobra is the name of a mythical serpent. It is believed to protect the sacred city of Mecca, and its venom has healing properties. The name Kobra carries the meaning “Venomous serpent” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kobra usually hope their child will grow to embody venomous serpent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Kobra" in popular culture has evolved beyond the mere description of a mythical snake. It has been adopted as a nickname or title in various contexts, often symbolizing power, strength, and mystery. For instance, it is used as a name for certain musical groups, traditional Arabic dances, or even as a term of endearment.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic mythology, the Kobra snake is a symbol of spiritual power, resilience, and protection. It is believed that the snake was created before other creatures, and it guards the sacred town of Mecca in Saudi Arabia. Its venom, instead of being lethal, has miraculous healing properties. Thus, it reflects the concept of transforming potential adversity into blessings. Moreover, the serpent's association with Mecca highlights the idea that the divine power and healing potency are accessible to those who seek spiritual refuge and purification.
